title: Desk: daily macro analysis + longer-horizon macro/event trades -- design the brief (format, inputs, sources), then test whether it changes trading net of cost
note:
OPERATOR REQUEST 2026-11-25 ~15:20Z (verbatim intent): a daily macro analysis as a trading-desk task. Work out the FORMAT, WHAT it looks at, WHICH SOURCES, and WHAT information it gives the operator. TEST how it might affect our trading. Look at LONGER-TERM trades made on macro events or conditions: both scheduled ones (interest rates, earnings) and unscheduled ones (a big CEO resigning, a new technology being proven, etc.).

SCOPE (build order; each step a commit or unit, never a memo):
1. DESIGN, before any code: a one-page brief spec. (a) The daily output: regime/condition summary, calendar for the next 1-5 sessions (rates/CPI/NFP/FOMC, earnings for rostered symbols and index heavyweights), overnight unscheduled-event digest, what it implies for each open or rostered leg, and candidate longer-horizon trade ideas, each with a falsifiable thesis and an invalidation level. (b) The input list with point-in-time availability. (c) The source list: what we already have (comms/macro/, config/macro_*.yaml, the econ/event calendar from DESK-EVENT-CALENDAR, COT, funding, Bigdata.com news/events/sentiment via MCP, live web reads from DESK-14), plus gaps. (d) The decision interface: advice-only to the desk; it never changes an order by itself.
2. PROTOTYPE the daily brief as a desk routine (trading-desk skill), writing comms/desk/macro/<date>.json + a readable render. Advice-only.
3. TEST effect on trading, offline first (macro-research skill invariants: point-in-time, no lookahead, beat the naive floor, net of the full cost stack). (a) Scheduled-event conditioning: do existing legs' outcomes differ around rate decisions or earnings? Reuse IR-MACRO-ANNDAY-POOLED and DESK-18G-EVENT-ENTRIES; don't duplicate them. (b) Unscheduled-event study: build a point-in-time event set (CEO departures, tech/product proof events) from news archives, then measure abnormal returns at 1d/5d/20d horizons per event class, net of cost. Pre-register each class as a research/queue unit before the run. (c) A longer-horizon macro trade arm: days-to-weeks holds, pre-registered rule, graded under the Stage-0 ladder (OPERATING-PLAN s2), like any leg.
4. If a test passes: the normal ladder (a Stage-0 pass goes to real money per OPERATING-PLAN s2). If not, the next iteration from the diagnosis (no giving up; regime is a standing lever, REGIME-PROGRAM).

RELATED ROWS to read first: DESK-14-LIVE-WEB-CONTEXT, DESK-18G-EVENT-ENTRIES, DESK-EVENT-CALENDAR, IR-MACRO-ANNDAY-POOLED, D3-POINT-IN-TIME-MACRO-BUILDER, REGIME-PROGRAM. Skills: trading-desk, macro-research. No new gates; advice-only until its own net-of-cost test passes (active-management doctrine). Next command: read the related rows and the two skills, then write step 1's spec as a PR for the manager. OPERATOR CLARIFICATION 2026-11-25 ~15:30Z, the GOAL (supersedes any reading of this row as 'a report'): 'the goal here is for it to give trades basically ... or to give information that informs other trades.' And: 'This should basically be like the Claude version that will teach those models how to work better.'

So the design is TEACHER -> STUDENT:
(1) PRIMARY OUTPUT = TRADES: each daily brief emits concrete, pre-specified trade proposals (symbol, side, entry, stop, a real predictive TP per the TP doctrine, horizon), plus 'informs' tags that modify existing legs (e.g. avoid/size-down around an event). They are recorded and graded like any desk proposal (DESK-9-GRADING / DESK-20-OUTCOME-JOIN), so Claude's macro judgement gets a measured hit rate net of cost.
(2) TEACHER FOR THE MACRO SLEEVE: the macro sleeve (M28 value / M29 system-dynamics; MACRO-RESHAPE was dropped, so it hasn't been worked on in a while) is re-opened through this. Claude's daily structured judgements (regime call, per-asset macro tilt, event read) are logged point-in-time as LABELS and FEATURES that the sleeve's models can be trained on and checked against.
(3) TEACHER FOR THE NEWS MODEL: NEWS-ALPHA-PROGRAM (queued) and the news-analysis model. Claude's per-event classification (event class, direction, magnitude, horizon, confidence) on the same news items becomes a supervised target / distillation set for the news model, and its graded outcomes tell the news model which event classes actually move prices. Pattern: Claude decides now (expensive, slow, broad context); the cheap model learns to reproduce the decisions that GRADED WELL (DESK-19-STUDENT-HANDOFF is the existing desk student pattern; reuse it).
Build implication for step 1's spec: the brief's schema must be machine-readable and point-in-time from day 1 (every judgement timestamped, with sources cited and no later edits), because its value as a teacher depends on clean labels. Rows to read in addition: NEWS-ALPHA-PROGRAM, NEWS-ALPHA-FEATURES, MACRO-RESHAPE (why dropped), DESK-19-STUDENT-HANDOFF, DESK-9-GRADING.
